title: perf-bench-latency-log-olivia-khan-2026-03-04
content:
Quick notes and raw run logs from today (scratchpad)

Goal:
- Baseline latency/throughput for new dynamic-batching change + KV cache sticky sessions. Check tail latency impact for interactive chat workload.

Environment:
- Model: rw-3b-v1 (float16)
- Runtime: local dev cluster (dedicated-seq), GPU: A100 40GB, driver DL kernel v2.1
- Serving binary: inference-runtime v1.14.2-rc (with dynamic batching opt-in)
- Config snapshot: batcher.max_batch_size=64, batcher.timeout_ms=8, kvcache.enabled=true, kvcache.stickiness=0.75, quantization=none
- Workload: simulated chat traffic (mix of short/long): 70% short (prompt+completion avg tokens 60), 30% long (avg tokens 512)
- Load generator: locust-based harness, 200 concurrent clients, ramp 60s

Runs (raw):
1) Baseline (no dynamic batching change, kvcache ON)
- batcher.timeout_ms=12, max_batch_size=64
- p50: 48ms, p95: 220ms, p99: 520ms
- throughput: 42k tokens/s aggregate
- notes: kvcache hit ~34%, short queries dominated batches (smaller effective batch sizes)

2) Dynamic batching enabled (timeout 8ms)
- p50: 44ms, p95: 180ms, p99: 460ms
- throughput: 48k tokens/s
- notes: better throughput, tail improved but still some p99 spikes during long request bursts

3) Dynamic batching + stickier KV cache (stickiness=0.9)
- p50: 40ms, p95: 165ms, p99: 420ms
- throughput: 49.5k tokens/s
- kvcache hit: ~46% (estimate from runtime metrics)
- notes: tail reduced; single long request still causes p99 spike ~600ms every ~12k requests (some GC/IO observed)

4) Aggressive batch timeout (timeout 4ms)
- p50: 38ms, p95: 210ms, p99: 700ms
- throughput: 50k tokens/s (slight increase), but tail got worse (higher p95/p99)
- notes: lower timeout = smaller latency for p50 but increases head-of-line/inefficient batching for long requests -> p99 suffers

Quick observations:
- Dynamic batching (8ms) = win for throughput and p95; p99 still sensitive to long request interference.
- Increasing KV cache stickiness improved hit rate and lowered tail; likely because repeated chat turns hit the same KV shards and avoid recomputation.
- Too aggressive timeout reduces batching efficiency for mixed-length workload -> harmful for p99.
- There are periodic p99 spikes correlated with a background checkpointing job (see logs) and occasional CUDA memory defrag events at ~03:12:xx. Need to correlate with SRE cron jobs.

Immediate next steps / TODOs:
- Re-run 3) with longer-run (30m) to verify stability and measure hit-rate convergence (today runs were 8-10m).
- Add run with quantized model (int8) to estimate token-cost vs latency tradeoff.
- Add per-shard GC and cuda-mem logs to linked_artifacts for correlation.
- Open Jira for 'p99 spikes during long request bursts' (JIRA-1987) and tag SRE for checkpoint correlation.
- Share summary with Jamie and Sam, propose canary rollout config: batcher.timeout_ms=8, kvcache.stickiness=0.9 for hosted-prod (low-risk)

Rough conclusions for notes doc / deck:
- Recommendation: enable dynamic batching default with 8ms timeout and increase KV cache stickiness for chat-serving profiles. Monitor p99 aggressively and add guardrails (circuit breaker to fall back to smaller batch path) to handle long-request storm.

Random scratch thoughts:
- Maybe try adaptive timeout: start with 8ms, if long-request fraction > 20% then increase timeout to 12ms to protect p99. Could instrument client-level hints for 'long' requests.
- Consider preemptive KV eviction for low-access keys to keep hot shard smaller.

Attached artifacts (local):
- perf-0304-olivia-plot.png (p50/p95/p99 lines)
- perf-0304-olivia-raw.csv (raw time series)

End of scratchpad. Will polish into a short one-pager if runs hold on longer run.
